headline: Interpretable ADMET models and simulated binding data target peptides and macrocycles
label: Peptide Admet Prediction Resources
summary: Preprints on cyclic peptide ADMET, simulated peptide binding data and PTM-aware drug response appear alongside updated ADMET databases for ADCs and drugs.
synthesis: The dominant thread is machine learning for peptide and macrocycle pharmacology, with interpretability and data supply as the main concerns. AIO targets ADMET prediction for cyclic peptides and macrocycles with an interpretable multimodal framework using solvent-aware contrastive pretraining. VReceptor simulates sequence-dependent peptide binding data via pharmacophore-inspired weighting, as a source of training data. PTM-BDL is adjacent rather than peptide-specific: it combines typed PTM states with sequence, structure and drug features to predict drug response, with site-level integrated-gradients attributions. ADCdb 2.0 (542 antibody-drug conjugates) and DrugMAP 3.0 are reference databases that add ADMET endpoints alongside clinical or bioactivity data. The summaries do not show these resources being combined with the models.
